html:
Svetitskhoveli Cathedral is an Orthodox cathedral in Mtskheta, the ancient capital of Georgia, northwest of Tbilisi. The present building was raised between 1010 and 1029 by the architect Arsukisdze, on the site of a 4th-century church, and it is a masterpiece of medieval Georgian building.

Its name means "the life-giving pillar". Tradition says that the robe of Christ, brought from Jerusalem by a Georgian Jew, was buried here, and that a cedar grew from the grave. After the conversion of Georgia under King Mirian III, the first church was built on the spot.

The cathedral was built soon after the Georgian lands were united under the Bagrationi kings. It is a large cross-shaped church with a tall drum and dome and carved stone on its outer walls. For centuries it was the seat of the head of the Georgian Church and the place where kings were crowned and buried. With the other old churches of Mtskheta it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
